Diagnosis: Walk omits GET /foo/bar when a real handler shares the node created by Route’s synthetic mount stub; the regression reproduces this, while GET /foo/bar/{id} remains visible (tree_test.go:526-558; tree.go:628-640). 
Rejected hypothesis: The nested subrouter is not missing and path concatenation is not the cause, because the child route is enumerated correctly as GET /foo/bar/{id}.
Verified invariant: Route mounts install wildcard/stub routing state and attach subroutes, and Walk recursively visits attached subroutes while propagating middleware (mux.go:295-340; tree.go:628-640).
Untested invariant: Enumeration must retain a real same-pattern method handler while suppressing only the synthetic stub, including non-comparable handler implementations.
Unresolved gap: The production fix still needs an identity-safe way to distinguish the synthetic stub handler from a user handler without comparing non-comparable interface values.
Graph question: Which construction and traversal edges identify the synthetic mount stub separately from a real handler at the same node?
